items.claim: Security misconfiguration occurs at any stack layer (servers, frameworks, cloud storage, IaC) and yields vulnerabilities from default credentials, verbose errors, missing hardening, and over-permissive permissions.
items.body: Misconfiguration is pervasive: unhandled error messages leaking stack traces/framework versions, default or sample accounts left enabled, unnecessary features and debug endpoints active in production, weak TLS, missing security headers, and cloud storage or IaC resources exposed to the internet (e.g., S3 buckets with public read/write, security groups 0.0.0.0/0). CWE-16 is the Configuration category mapping to OWASP A05:2021. Prevention: repeatable hardening/security baselines, minimal platforms, identical environment configuration with different credentials, automated configuration review, and IAM least privilege. Detection happens via DAST, IaC scanning (Trivy, Checkov/tfsec), kube-bench, and CSPM.
items.disproof: If a baseline hardening standard is enforced and verified across all environments; if no default credentials remain; if debug endpoints and unnecessary features are removed; if security headers and TLS are set to secure values; and if misconfigured resources are caught by automated scanners before deployment, the risk is neutralized. A passing automated misconfiguration check across all layers disproves an exploitable configuration flaw.

sources.quote: Security misconfiguration is when a system, application, or cloud service is set up incorrectly from a security perspective, creating vulnerabilities.
This entry is a Category, but various sources map to it anyway, despite CWE guidance that Categories should not be mapped. In this case, there are no clear CWE Weaknesses that can be utilized.
Misconfigurations arise from how systems are set up: default credentials left in place, unnecessary features enabled, verbose errors, missing hardening, and overly permissive access.
